- **`pkg/agent/agent.go:689-693`** — the message is appended to history and the turn loop continues, so the model sees the refusal and can adapt instead of the run dying.

**Answer:** `pkg/agent/agent.go:1138` — `buildToolResultMsg` formats any non-nil tool error (including `permission.ErrDenied`) into a `RoleTool` message with the frozen `tool error: ` prefix, which the agent loop appends to the transcript at `agent.go:691` and then proceeds to the next model turn, making a denial a readable tool result rather than a fatal error.

The mechanism is deliberately generic, with no special-casing for denials:

1. **`internal/permission/permission.go:600`** defines `ErrDenied`. Tools call `Policy.Check` and return that error verbatim — e.g. `internal/tools/bash/bash.go:271` (`return "", err`), after optionally appending a plan-mode `Hint:`.
2. **`pkg/agent/agent.go:672-684`** — the tool-dispatch loop (both the concurrent read-only branch and the sequential mutating branch) funnels every `(result, terr)` pair into `buildToolResultMsg`.
3. **`pkg/agent/agent.go:1133-1140`** — that function builds a `deepseek.Message{Role: RoleTool, ToolCallID: callID}` and, if `terr != nil`, sets `msg.Content = ToolErrorPrefix + fmt.Sprint(terr)`. The message is appended to the transcript and sent back to the model on the next turn; the loop never propagates a tool error as fatal.

So a denial reaches the model as `tool error: permission denied: user declined bash` — the same shape as any other tool failure, which is why `internal/friction/friction.go:109` can score denials by prefix-matching that wire format. The tool-side complement is `bash.go:266-269`, which enriches the plan-analyze denial before it becomes that tool result.

**`internal/tools/references/references.go:151`** — `degradeMessage` converts three LSP-client failures into non-fatal "fall back to grep" tool results: a missing server binary in `PATH` (:155), a server timeout / `DeadlineExceeded` (:159, "may still be indexing"), and any other resolver error such as "no LSP server configured" or an init failure (:162); only `context.Canceled` is propagated as a real error (:157).

One sentence: references degrades when the language server is unavailable or failed — never for a genuine interrupt.

`internal/tools/references/references.go:151` — `degradeMessage`, called at `references.go:113` when `resolver.References` errors, converts the failure into a model-actionable tool result suggesting grep in three cases: a missing language-server binary (`MissingBinaryError`, line 155, with install hint), a `context.DeadlineExceeded` timeout such as a still-indexing server (line 159), and any other error such as "no LSP server configured for .rs files" or init failure (line 162) — with only `context.Canceled` propagated as a real error (line 156) rather than degraded.

**Mechanism:** `degradeMessage` at `internal/tools/references/references.go:151` — called from `Execute` at `references.go:113` when `resolver.References` returns an error.

**One sentence:** The tool degrades to a grep hint in exactly three cases — the language server binary is missing from PATH (`references.go:155`), the LSP call hit `context.DeadlineExceeded` while indexing (`references.go:159`), or any other resolver error such as "no LSP server configured for .rs files" or an init failure (`references.go:162`) — while `context.Canceled` (Esc/user interrupt) is deliberately propagated as a real error instead (`references.go:156-157`), so it never becomes a "fall back to grep" message.

The key design point: these are returned as **normal tool results** (`nil` error), not failures, so the model sees actionable structured text rather than a `ToolExecEnd` failure and can immediately switch strategy.

I'll locate the fallback logic in the references tool.**`internal/tools/references/references.go:151`** — `degradeMessage` (called from `Execute` at `references.go:113` whenever `resolver.References` returns an error) swallows any LSP failure into a non-fatal `[references: … Fall back to grep.]` tool result, except a genuine `context.Canceled` interrupt, which it re-propagates as a real error.

The three degrading branches:

| Condition | Line | Message shape |
|---|---|---|
| Server binary missing from `PATH` (`*lspclient.MissingBinaryError`, raised by `manager.go:110` via `exec.LookPath`) | `references.go:154-155` | says which server + `install: …` + "Fall back to grep for now." |
| `context.DeadlineExceeded` (server still indexing) | `references.go:158-159` | "timed out … Try again shortly, or fall back to grep." |
| Everything else — unsupported extension (`no LSP server configured for .rs files`, `manager.go:122`) and init/JSON-RPC failures | `references.go:161-162` | `%v. Fall back to grep.` |

So the degradation is "any resolver error that isn't an Esc/turn cancellation" — cancellation stays a fatal error so the interrupt isn't masked as a hint. The same conditions are advertised to the model up-front in the tool's `description` (`references.go:41`: "Needs the language server on PATH; if it's missing, or the project doesn't type-check, fall back to grep").
